claims.text: Lowering the Cu content of an FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coating will reduce its high-temperature wear rate.
Lowering Cu content diminishes tensile-compression asymmetry in FeNiCrCoCu.
Tensile-compression asymmetry is tied to enhanced nano-twinning and differences in dislocation slip at the coating-substrate interface.
Fe33Ni32Cr11Co11Cu13 is a representative baseline FeNiCrCoCu composition.
Substituting some Cu with Fe will lower the alloy's propensity for nano-twinning.
The proposed mechanism applies to high-temperature wear at approximately 400-600 °C.
The proposed mechanism applies under high-load sliding or contact stress.
Overall wear resistance is governed by coating-substrate interfacial integrity and the density and distribution of twins and dislocation-slip zones.
Increasing temperature increases tensile-compression asymmetry in FeNiCrCoCu.
Increasing Cu content increases tensile-compression asymmetry in FeNiCrCoCu.
At elevated temperature, increased Cu promotes nano-twinning during compression.
At elevated temperature, increased Cu reduces dislocation slip during tension.
Cu-induced differences between compressive twinning and tensile slip produce localized strain and stress concentrations at the coating-substrate interface.
Reducing Cu produces more uniform plastic deformation.
More uniform plastic deformation and reduced interfacial stress localization lead to less wear.
Cu-reduced coatings will exhibit fewer nano-twins relative to dislocation activity than the baseline coating.
Cu-reduced coatings will exhibit improved coating-substrate interface integrity.
The mechanism may not hold at room temperature or under low loads because different wear mechanisms may prevail.
Oxidation and substrate-induced stress may also affect high-temperature wear performance.
